mainTopic: צדיקים and בינונים, רבי עקיבא's מסירות נפש for ״בכל נפשך״, and respect for the direction of the מקדש
overview: The amud opens by finishing a list of what each organ does, then sorts people into צדיקים, רשעים, and בינונים by which יצר rules them. רבה calls himself a בינוני and אביי protests. רבא and רב add that each world belongs to one extreme: אחאב gets עולם הזה, and רבי חנינא בן דוסא gets עולם הבא. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's פסוק ״ואהבת את ה׳ אלהיך״. רבי אליעזר explains why it says both ״בכל נפשך״ and ״בכל מאדך״, and רבי עקיבא teaches that ״בכל נפשך״ means even if He takes your life. A long story follows: רבי עקיבא teaches תורה despite Rome's decree, explains himself with the משל of the fox and the fish, and dies saying שמע with his soul leaving at the word אחד. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה's rule about respect toward the מקדש. It limits that rule, then brings two ברייתות about which direction one may face when relieving oneself. The amud ends with רבה, who follows רבי עקיבא's view that it is forbidden everywhere.

steps.title: The jobs of the body's organs
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues its list of organs and gives each one a job: drinking, anger, calming, laughter, grinding, sleep, and waking.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lungs draw in all kinds of liquids. The liver gets angry. The gall bladder drops a drop of gall into the liver and calms it. The spleen laughs. The maw grinds the food. The stomach brings sleep. The nose wakes a person up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא, started on the previous עמוד, that lists what each part of the body does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each organ gets one job, including emotional jobs like anger and laughter. The liver and the gall bladder work as a pair: one makes anger and the other calms it. The last two, stomach and nose, are also a pair, sleep and waking, and the next steps build on that pair.

keyTerms.meaning: Maw / gizzard, the organ that grinds food

phrases.english: The lung draws in all kinds of liquids,
the liver gets angry,
the gall bladder throws a drop into it and calms it,
phrases.notes: "בּוֹ" means into the liver. The drop of gall settles the anger.

phrases.english: the spleen laughs,
the maw grinds,
the stomach brings sleep,
the nose awakens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of organs begun earlier on the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each organ has its own job; the stomach brings sleep and the nose wakes a person.

steps.title: If the sleep organ and the waking organ swap jobs
steps.stepSummary: If the organ of sleep wakes and the organ of waking brings sleep, the person slowly wastes away.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the one that brings sleep wakes, or the one that wakes brings sleep, the person slowly wastes away.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds what happens if the sleep organ and the waking organ (stomach and nose) switch roles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Health depends on each organ doing its own job. If the two swap, the body gets confused, and the person weakens slowly instead of dying at once.

phrases.english: If the sleeping one wakes, or the waking one sleeps —
phrases.notes: This refers to the stomach and the nose from the previous step.

phrases.english: he gradually wastes away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the sleep and waking pair from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the roles are reversed, the person slowly deteriorates.

steps.title: If both organs sleep or both wake
steps.stepSummary: A further teaching says that if both organs bring sleep, or both wake, the person dies right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if both bring sleep, or both wake, he dies immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching (תנא) about the sleep and waking organs, describing an even worse case than a swap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a swap, there is still one organ for sleep and one for waking, just in the wrong places, so the person declines slowly. If both do the same job, the balance is completely gone, and death is immediate.

phrases.english: It was taught: if both of them bring sleep
or both of them awaken —
he dies immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a more extreme case to the swap case in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If both organs share one role, death is immediate.

steps.title: Who rules a person: יצר טוב, יצר רע, or both
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי says the יצר טוב rules צדיקים, the יצר רע rules רשעים, and both rule בינונים, with a פסוק for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught that רבי יוסי הגלילי says: the good inclination rules the righteous, as it says, "And my heart is empty within me." The evil inclination rules the wicked, as it says, "Transgression speaks to the wicked within my heart; there is no fear of God before his eyes." Middle people are ruled by both, as it says, "He stands at the right hand of the needy, to save him from those who judge his soul."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the body's organs to the inner forces in a person's heart, quoting a ברייתא that sorts people into three groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link to the previous section is the heart and the inner organs. A צדיק has emptied his heart (חלל) of the יצר רע, a רשע is controlled by sin, and a בינוני has two "judges" (שופטי, plural) pulling at him.

keyTerms.meaning: Middle people, neither fully righteous nor fully wicked
Empty / hollow (here, emptied of the יצר רע)

steps.confusionAlert: In this ברייתא, בינוני simply means someone pulled by both inclinations. Don't import other definitions of בינוני from other books (such as תניא) into the plain meaning here.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
The righteous — the good inclination rules them,
as it is said: "And my heart is empty within me" (Psalms 109:22).
phrases.notes: The heart is emptied of the evil inclination.

phrases.english: The wicked — the evil inclination rules them,
as it is said: "Transgression speaks to the wicked within my heart,
there is no fear of God before his eyes" (Psalms 36:2).
Middle people — both this and that rule them,
as it is said: "He stands at the right hand of the needy,
to save him from those who judge his soul" (Psalms 109:31).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from physical organs to the inclinations within the heart.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדיקים are ruled by the יצר טוב, רשעים by the יצר רע, and בינונים by both.
steps.whyThisMatters: This three-part sorting of people frames everything that follows: רבה, אביי, רבא, and רב all build on it.

steps.title: רבה calls himself a בינוני
steps.stepSummary: רבה humbly says that people like himself are בינונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: people like us are middle people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה applies the ברייתא to himself and says he is only a בינוני. This sets up אביי's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a great אמורא saw himself as someone still struggling between the two inclinations.

keyTerms.meaning: Such as us / people like us

phrases.english: Rabba said: people like us are middle people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the categories of step 4 to real people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה classifies himself as a בינוני.

steps.title: אביי protests רבה's humility
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects: if a great man like רבה is only a בינוני, no one else stands a chance.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Master, you are not leaving life for any creature!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי, רבה's student and nephew, pushes back against רבה's claim that he is only a בינוני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sentence is shaped as a question, but it works as a challenge. If someone as great as רבה is merely middle, then everyone else must be wicked, and no one would deserve to live.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא שָׁבֵיק מָר חַיֵּי לְכׇל בְּרִיָּה?
phrases.english: Does the Master not leave life for any creature?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical protest, not a real question.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שָׁבֵיק מָר חַיֵּי לְכׇל בְּרִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's statement in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that he is only a בינוני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the greatest people are only middle, everyone lesser has no merit left to live by.

steps.title: The world was made for the fully wicked or the fully righteous
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the world was created only for the completely wicked or the completely righteous.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: the world was created only for the completely wicked or the completely righteous.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new teaching about the extremes: only the two complete types truly get a full world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each extreme gets one full world. The רשע gets עולם הזה, and the צדיק gets עולם הבא. The בינוני does not enjoy either one completely. Step 9 spells this out with examples.

phrases.english: And Rava said: the world was not created
except for the completely wicked
or for the completely righteous.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: לָא אִיבְּרִי עָלְמָא אֶלָּא לְרַשִּׁיעֵי גְּמוּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the three types by focusing on the two extremes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Full enjoyment of a world belongs only to the completely wicked or the completely righteous.

steps.title: A person should know whether he is completely righteous
steps.stepSummary: רבא says a person knows within himself whether or not he is a צדיק גמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: a person should know in himself whether he is completely righteous or not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds that each person can tell which group he is in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On one explanation, someone who is not a צדיק גמור knows to expect hardship in this life. This step ties the abstract categories to a person's own awareness of himself.

phrases.english: Rava said: a person should know in himself

phrases.aramaic: אִם צַדִּיק גָּמוּר הוּא אִם לָאו.
phrases.english: whether he is completely righteous or not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 7 to the individual's knowledge of himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person can know whether he is a צדיק גמור.

steps.title: אחאב and רבי חנינא בן דוסא: one world each
steps.stepSummary: רב says the world was created only for אחאב בן עמרי and רבי חנינא בן דוסא. אחאב gets עולם הזה, and רבי חנינא בן דוסא gets עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: the world was created only for אחאב בן עמרי and for רבי חנינא בן דוסא. For אחאב בן עמרי, עולם הזה; for רבי חנינא בן דוסא, עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives two real examples of the extremes, then explains which world belongs to each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This puts רבא's idea from step 7 into concrete terms. אחאב, a complete רשע, enjoyed full luxury in עולם הזה. רבי חנינא בן דוסא, a complete צדיק, lived in poverty but has the full עולם הבא.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three types of people: צדיקים (ruled by the יצר טוב), רשעים (ruled by the יצר רע), and בינונים (ruled by both). Only the extremes receive one full world: the רשע like אחאב gets עולם הזה, and the צדיק like רבי חנינא בן דוסא gets עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Rav said: the world was not created
except for Ahab son of Omri
and for Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa.
For Ahab son of Omri — this world,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא — הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: and for Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa — the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לָא אִיבְּרִי עָלְמָא אֶלָּא לְאַחְאָב בֶּן עָמְרִי וּלְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives concrete examples of רבא's two extremes from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולם הזה was made for אחאב, the complete רשע; עולם הבא was made for רבי חנינא בן דוסא, the complete צדיק.

steps.title: Returning to the verse of loving God
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's verse ״ואהבת את ה׳ אלהיך״ to open a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And you shall love the Lord your God."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new section by quoting the פסוק that the משנה explained. The next steps will explain this פסוק more fully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the פרק, the משנה explained each part of this פסוק: ״בכל לבבך״, ״בכל נפשך״ and ״בכל מאדך״. Now the גמרא comes back to that משנה to bring a ברייתא that explains it further. This line is only a heading. It does not make an argument by itself.

phrases.english: "And you shall love the Lord your God."
phrases.notes: Quoting the פסוק that the משנה explained (דברים ו:ה).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of צדיקים and רשעים and returns to the משנה's explanation of this פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heading line that introduces the explanation of ״ואהבת את ה׳ אלהיך״.

steps.title: Why does the Torah need both 'soul' and 'might'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks why the פסוק says both ״בכל נפשך״ and ״בכל מאדך״, since each seems to make the other unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר says: If the תורה already says "with all your soul," why does it also say "with all your might"? And if it says "with all your might," why does it also say "with all your soul"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר asks a question about extra words in the פסוק. He is setting up his own answer, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you must give up your life for ה׳, then giving up your money is obviously included, so ״מאדך״ seems extra. If you must give up all your money, it seems the תורה could have said only that one. The question works both ways, so each phrase must teach something the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: With all your soul, meaning even your life
With all your might, meaning all your money and possessions

steps.confusionAlert: Here ״מאדך״ does not mean physical strength. חז״ל read it as 'your money' or 'your possessions.'

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If it is stated "with all your soul,"
why does it state "with all your might"?
And if it is stated "with all your might,"
why does it state "with all your soul"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם נֶאֱמַר ״בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ״, לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר ״בְּכָל מְאֹדֶךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the פסוק quoted in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק need both phrases, if each one seems to include or replace the other?

steps.title: Different people value different things
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that some people care more about their body and others care more about their money, so the תורה speaks to each type.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: if there is a person whose body is dearer to him than his money, that is why it says "with all your soul." And if there is a person whose money is dearer to him than his body, that is why it says "with all your might."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers his own question. Each phrase speaks to a different kind of person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither phrase is 'obviously included' in the other, because people are different. For one person, giving up money is easy and giving up life is the big test. For another person, money is the bigger test. The תורה demands that each person be ready to give up the thing he holds dearest.

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a person
whose body is dearer to him than his money,
that is why it says "with all your soul."
And if there is a person
whose money is dearer to him than his body,
that is why it says "with all your might."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִם יֵשׁ לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁגּוּפוֹ חָבִיב עָלָיו מִמָּמוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both phrases are needed, because different people treasure either their body or their money more.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: even if He takes your soul
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains that ״בכל נפשך״ means you must love ה׳ even when your life is being taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: "With all your soul" means even if He takes your soul.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives his own explanation of ״בכל נפשך״. He sets the highest level of love: loving ה׳ even at the moment of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר focused on which thing a person values more. רבי עקיבא focuses on how far the love must go: all the way, even while your life is being taken. The story that follows shows רבי עקיבא living out this very teaching.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is the background for the story that follows, which shows רבי עקיבא's own self-sacrifice for תורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
"With all your soul" means even if He takes your soul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second explanation of ״בכל נפשך״, alongside רבי אליעזר's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״בכל נפשך״ means loving ה׳ even while one's life is being taken.

steps.title: פפוס asks רבי עקיבא if he is not afraid
steps.stepSummary: Rome forbids learning תורה. פפוס בן יהודה finds רבי עקיבא teaching in public and asks if he is not afraid of the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Once, the wicked kingdom decreed that the Jews may not engage in תורה. פפוס בן יהודה came and found רבי עקיבא gathering crowds in public and learning תורה. He said to him: עקיבא, are you not afraid of the government?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story in a ברייתא. פפוס challenges רבי עקיבא for openly breaking the decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question sounds like a simple question, but it is really a challenge: openly teaching seems reckless. It sets up רבי עקיבא's answer, which explains why stopping תורה would be even more dangerous.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: One time
the wicked kingdom decreed
that Israel may not engage in Torah.
Pappos ben Yehuda came
and found Rabbi Akiva
gathering crowds in public
and engaging in Torah.
He said to him: Akiva,
are you not afraid of the government?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story showing how רבי עקיבא lived his teaching of ״בכל נפשך״.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's public teaching of תורה during the decree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Openly breaking the Roman decree seems to put his life in needless danger.

steps.title: The parable of the fox and the fish
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers with a משל: a fox sees fish fleeing from nets and invites them onto dry land to live with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I will give you a parable. What is this like? A fox was walking along the riverbank and saw fish gathering and rushing from place to place. He said to them: What are you running from? They said: From the nets that people bring upon us. He said to them: Would you like to come up onto dry land, and we will live together, just as my ancestors lived with your ancestors?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא begins answering פפוס with a משל. This step sets up the scene; the punchline comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fish stand for the Jewish people, the nets for Rome's danger, and the water for תורה. The fox's 'kind' offer stands for the temptation to escape danger by leaving תורה. Leaving the water seems safe but is really deadly.

phrases.english: He said to him: I will tell you a parable.
What is this like?

phrases.aramaic: לְשׁוּעָל שֶׁהָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ עַל גַּב הַנָּהָר,
phrases.english: A fox walking along the riverbank
saw fish
gathering and fleeing from place to place.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: מִפְּנֵי מָה אַתֶּם בּוֹרְחִים?
phrases.english: He said to them: What are you fleeing from?
They said to him: From nets
that people bring upon us.
He said to them: Would you like to come up onto dry land,
and you and I will live together,
just as my ancestors lived with your ancestors?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶמְשׁוֹל לְךָ מָשָׁל, לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא begins answering פפוס's challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Introduces the משל that will explain why leaving תורה is not a real escape.

steps.title: The fish reject the fox's offer
steps.stepSummary: The fish call the fox a fool: if they are afraid in the water where they live, they would surely die on land.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Are you the one they call the cleverest of animals? You are not clever, you are a fool! If we are afraid in the place that keeps us alive, then in the place where we would die, how much more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The fish turn down the fox's offer. They explain with a קל וחומר why leaving the water is foolish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fish agree that the water has dangers, but land means certain death. A risky life is better than a guaranteed death. This is the turning point of the משל.

keyTerms.meaning: How much more so (a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: They said to him: Are you the one
they call the cleverest of the animals?!

phrases.aramaic: לֹא פִּקֵּחַ אַתָּה, אֶלָּא טִפֵּשׁ אַתָּה!
phrases.english: You are not clever; you are a fool!
If in the place that keeps us alive we are afraid,

phrases.aramaic: בִּמְקוֹם מִיתָתֵנוּ — עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה.
phrases.english: in the place of our death, how much more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא פִּקֵּחַ אַתָּה, אֶלָּא טִפֵּשׁ אַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Inside the משל, the fish reject the fox's proposal from step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The fox's offer to leave the water
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Leaving the water, their source of life, means certain death, which is far worse than the danger of the nets.

steps.title: The lesson: Torah is our life
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא applies the משל: תורה is our 'water.' If we are in danger while learning, we would be in far greater danger if we stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too us: now, while we sit and learn תורה, about which it is written "For it is your life and the length of your days," we are in this much danger. If we go and stop learning it, how much more so!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא explains the meaning of the משל. This is his real answer to פפוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as water is the fish's life, the פסוק calls תורה our life. Danger while learning תורה is real, but abandoning תורה is spiritual death. So fear of Rome is no reason to stop learning.
steps.whatToRemember: תורה is to the Jewish people what water is to fish. Leaving it to escape danger is not safety; it is death.

phrases.english: So too we, now,
while we sit and engage in Torah,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּהּ: ״כִּי הוּא חַיֶּיךָ וְאֹרֶךְ יָמֶיךָ״,
phrases.english: about which it is written: "For it is your life and the length of your days,"

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ, אִם אָנוּ הוֹלְכִים וּמְבַטְּלִים מִמֶּנָּה —
phrases.english: are in this much danger; if we go and stop learning it,
how much more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנַחְנוּ עַכְשָׁיו שֶׁאָנוּ יוֹשְׁבִים וְעוֹסְקִים בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the fish's reasoning in step 16 to the Jewish people and תורה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Stopping תורה would be far more dangerous than learning it under the decree, because תורה is our life.

steps.title: Both men end up in prison
steps.stepSummary: A few days later, רבי עקיבא was arrested and imprisoned, and פפוס בן יהודה was arrested and put in prison next to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Only a few days passed before they seized רבי עקיבא and locked him in prison. They also seized פפוס בן יהודה and locked him up beside him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: both men are arrested. This sets up their conversation in prison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פפוס tried to stay safe, but he was arrested anyway. This shows the point of the משל: leaving תורה does not guarantee safety.

phrases.english: They said: Only a few days passed
until they seized Rabbi Akiva
and locked him in prison,
and they seized Pappos ben Yehuda
and locked him up beside him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after רבי עקיבא's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both רבי עקיבא and פפוס were arrested and imprisoned together.

steps.title: פפוס: fortunate is the one arrested for תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא asks פפוס why he is there. פפוס says רבי עקיבא is fortunate to be arrested for תורה, while he was arrested for meaningless things.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: פפוס, who brought you here? He answered: Fortunate are you, רבי עקיבא, that you were arrested for words of תורה. Woe to פפוס, who was arrested for empty matters.
steps.whatsHappening: In prison, פפוס admits that רבי עקיבא was right. This closes the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both men faced the same punishment, but only רבי עקיבא suffered for something holy. פפוס's suffering had no meaning. This confirms the lesson of the משל and of ״בכל נפשך״.
steps.whatToRemember: פפוס tried to avoid danger by staying away from תורה, yet he ended up in the same prison, with nothing to show for it. רבי עקיבא suffered for תורה, which made him 'fortunate.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: פַּפּוּס, מִי הֲבִיאֲךָ לְכָאן?
phrases.english: He said to him: Pappos, who brought you here?
He said to him: Fortunate are you, Rabbi Akiva,
for you were arrested for words of Torah.
Woe to Pappos,
who was arrested for empty matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁרֶיךָ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁנִּתְפַּסְתָּ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The prison conversation resolves the challenge פפוס raised in step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Suffering for תורה is a privilege. Avoiding תורה out of fear brings no real safety, only meaningless suffering.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא recites שמע while being tortured
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא is taken out to be killed at the time of קריאת שמע. While his flesh is torn with iron combs, he accepts עול מלכות שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they took רבי עקיבא out to be killed, it was the time for קריאת שמע. They were tearing his flesh with iron combs, and he was accepting upon himself the yoke of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of רבי עקיבא continues. He is now being executed, and even during the torture he says שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי עקיבא told פפוס that leaving תורה is more dangerous than keeping it. Now we see him live that out at the very end. Saying שמע is called accepting עול מלכות שמים, and he does it in the worst possible pain.

keyTerms.meaning: The yoke of Heaven's kingship, accepted by saying שמע
The daily reciting of the שמע

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לַהֲרִיגָה
phrases.english: At the time they took Rabbi Akiva out to be killed
it was the time for reciting Shema,
and they were combing (tearing) his flesh
with combs of iron,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה מְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם.
phrases.english: and he was accepting upon himself the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לַהֲרִיגָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after רבי עקיבא was arrested and imprisoned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא accepted עול מלכות שמים even while being tortured to death.

steps.title: The students ask: even now?
steps.stepSummary: His students ask how he can go on reciting שמע in such suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said to him: Our teacher, even to this point?!
steps.whatsHappening: The students are amazed and ask רבי עקיבא how he can keep saying שמע even now. This sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is short. It means: is this what מסירות נפש requires, even in such pain? It prepares the explanation of the פסוק בכל נפשך.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to this point? Even now?

phrases.english: His students said to him:
Our teacher, even to this point?!
phrases.notes: Meaning: even now, in this suffering?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: רַבֵּינוּ, עַד כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רבי עקיבא saying שמע during torture.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can he still accept עול מלכות שמים in such pain?

steps.title: רבי עקיבא explains בכל נפשך
steps.stepSummary: He explains that all his life he waited to fulfill 'with all your soul,' meaning even if God takes your life. Now that the chance has come, he will not miss it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: All my days I was troubled by this verse, 'with all your soul,' which means even if He takes your soul. I said: When will this come to me so I can fulfill it? Now that it has come, shall I not fulfill it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers his students. He sees this moment as his chance to fulfill a מצוה he had wanted to keep all his life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'ואהבת... בכל נפשך' is explained as loving ה' even at the cost of your life. רבי עקיבא worried his whole life that he might never get to keep this part. For him the torture is not only suffering. It is a rare opportunity.

keyTerms.meaning: With all your soul (from the שמע)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for how חז"ל understand בכל נפשך as giving one's life for ה'.

phrases.english: He said to them:
All my days I was troubled
by this verse: "with all your soul"
even if He takes your soul.
I said: When will it come to my hand so that I can fulfill it?
And now that it has come to my hand, shall I not fulfill it?

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל יָמַי הָיִיתִי מִצְטַעֵר עַל פָּסוּק זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He longed all his life to fulfill בכל נפשך, and now he finally can.

steps.title: His soul leaves at the word אחד
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא stretches out the word אחד until he dies, and a בת קול praises him for this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He stretched out the word 'One' until his soul left him on 'One.' A heavenly voice came out and said: 'Fortunate are you, רבי עקיבא, that your soul left you on One.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא dies while saying the word אחד, and a voice from Heaven praises him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחד is the key word of שמע, declaring that ה' is One. רבי עקיבא's final breath is that declaration. The בת קול confirms that Heaven sees this as a perfect ending.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One,' the last word of the first פסוק of שמע

phrases.english: He was prolonging the word "One,"
until his soul left him on "One."
A heavenly voice came out and said:
"Fortunate are you, Rabbi Akiva,
that your soul left you on 'One.'"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי עקיבא carrying out what he just explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא died declaring אחד, and Heaven praised him.

steps.title: The angels protest: is this the reward for תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The מלאכי השרת ask הקב"ה how such a death can be the reward for תורה, quoting 'ממתים ידך ה''.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ministering angels said before הקב"ה: This is תורה, and this is its reward? 'From death by Your hand, ה', from death...'!
steps.whatsHappening: The angels challenge הקב"ה, asking how a great תלמיד חכם could receive such a terrible death. This sets up הקב"ה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As רש״י explains, the angels read the פסוק to mean that a righteous person should die by ה''s hand, a natural death, and not by human hands with torture. They are not asking for information. They are protesting that the result seems unfair. Their question is the classic question of צדיק ורע לו.

keyTerms.meaning: This is תורה and this is its reward?
From death by Your hand (תהלים יז:יד)

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: The ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
This is Torah, and this is its reward?
"From death, by Your hand, O Lord, from death..." (Psalms 17:14)!
phrases.notes: As רש״י explains: he should have died by ה׳'s hand, not at the hands of people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the outcome of רבי עקיבא's death.
steps.kashyaTarget: The justice of רבי עקיבא's death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone who gave his life to תורה should have died by ה''s hand, not by human torture, as the פסוק suggests.

steps.title: הקב"ה answers: their portion is in life
steps.stepSummary: הקב"ה answers with the end of the same פסוק: 'their portion is in life,' meaning eternal life.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'Their portion is in life.'
steps.whatsHappening: הקב"ה answers the angels by quoting the rest of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angels quoted only the beginning of the פסוק. The end, 'חלקם בחיים,' shows that the true reward of the צדיק is in real, eternal life, not in this world. So his death does not cancel his reward.

keyTerms.meaning: Their portion is in life (the eternal life)

phrases.english: He said to them: "Their portion is in life."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the angels' protest.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Completing the verse: the same פסוק the angels quoted contains the answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק implies the צדיק should die only by ה''s hand, not a violent death at human hands.
steps.terutzMaskana: The צדיק's real portion is eternal life.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא is destined for עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול announces that רבי עקיבא is ready for life in עולם הבא. This ends the story.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said: 'Fortunate are you, רבי עקיבא, for you are destined for the life of עולם הבא.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a heavenly voice confirming that רבי עקיבא's reward is waiting for him in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This second בת קול spells out the meaning of 'חלקם בחיים.' The 'life' meant here is the life of עולם הבא. The angels' question is fully answered.

keyTerms.meaning: The life of the World to Come

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא died with מסירות נפש, fulfilling בכל נפשך while saying אחד. His reward is not in this world but in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said:
"Fortunate are you, Rabbi Akiva,
for you are destined for the life of the World to Come."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms and explains הקב"ה's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא's reward for his תורה and מסירות נפש is eternal life in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: respect toward the Eastern Gate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a person may not act lightheadedly facing שער המזרח, which lines up with the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person should not act lightheadedly opposite the Eastern Gate, which is lined up with the קודש הקדשים, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and the גמרא returns to the next line of the משנה. This quote sets up the limits that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says to behave respectfully in the direction of the בית המקדש, specifically toward שער המזרח, because it faces the קודש הקדשים. The next steps will narrow when this rule applies.

keyTerms.meaning: A person should not act lightheadedly (disrespectfully)
The Eastern Gate of הר הבית

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic made up by the גמרא. It is a quote from our משנה. The story of רבי עקיבא was a long side discussion, and now we are back to the משנה.

phrases.english: A person should not act lightheadedly
opposite the Eastern Gate

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא מְכוּוָּן כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: which is aligned with the Holy of Holies, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יָקֵל אָדָם אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ כְּנֶגֶד שַׁעַר הַמִּזְרָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must not behave disrespectfully facing שער המזרח, which lines up with the קודש הקדשים.

steps.title: רב limits the rule to the area of הצופים where one can see
steps.stepSummary: רב says the rule applies only from הר הצופים inward, and only where one can see the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: They only said this from הצופים and inward, and when he can see.
steps.whatsHappening: רב narrows the משנה's rule. It does not apply everywhere, only close to ירושלים where the מקדש is visible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sounds open-ended. רב adds two conditions: you must be inside the area of הצופים (Mount Scopus), and you must be able to see the מקדש. Without both, the rule does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: They only said (this rule) in the case of...
Mount Scopus, a lookout point from which the מקדש is first seen

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא מִן הַצּוֹפִים וְלִפְנִים,
phrases.english: They only said this from Mount Scopus and inward,
and when one can see (the Temple).

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא מִן הַצּוֹפִים וְלִפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prohibition applies only from הצופים inward, where the מקדש is visible.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the same and adds more conditions
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן also limits the rule to הצופים and seeing. He adds two more conditions: there is no fence blocking the view, and the שכינה rests there.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי אבא son of רבי חייא בר אבא said that רבי יוחנן said: They only said this from הצופים and inward, when one can see, when there is no fence, and at a time when the שכינה rests there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב from רבי יוחנן, who says the same thing and adds extra details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'איתמר נמי' means another אמורא said the same idea, so רב's limit is backed up. רבי יוחנן adds two conditions. First, nothing may block the view. Second, the rule applies only while the שכינה rests there, which means while the בית המקדש stands. So the rule is even narrower.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (support from another אמורא)
A fence or wall blocking the view
The Divine Presence rests (while the מקדש stands)

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, said:
This is what Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא מִן הַצּוֹפִים וְלִפְנִים,
phrases.english: They only said this from Mount Scopus and inward,
and when one can see, and when there is no fence,
and at a time when the Divine Presence rests there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's limit and adds further conditions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's parallel statement, as reported by רבי אבא

steps.title: ברייתא: which direction to face when relieving oneself
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that in יהודה one should face north-south when relieving oneself, not east-west. In the גליל, one should face only east-west.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One who relieves himself in יהודה should not face east and west, only north and south. In the גליל he should face only east and west.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא about respect for the direction of ירושלים when relieving oneself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is not to face toward ירושלים and the מקדש while doing something undignified. In יהודה, east-west would line up with ירושלים, so one faces north-south. The גליל is north of ירושלים, so north-south would face it, and there one faces east-west instead.
steps.confusionAlert: The allowed direction flips between יהודה and the גליל. The rule is not about east or west as such. It is about not facing ירושלים, and that depends on where you are standing.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who relieves himself in Judea
should not relieve himself facing east and west,
but rather north and south.

phrases.aramaic: וּבַגָּלִיל לֹא יִפָּנֶה אֶלָּא מִזְרָח וּמַעֲרָב.
phrases.english: And in the Galilee he should relieve himself only facing east and west.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא about respect for the direction of the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not relieve oneself facing toward ירושלים. The allowed direction depends on the region.

steps.title: רבי יוסי permits, under the same limits as רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי permits it. In his view the prohibition applies only when one can see the מקדש, there is no fence, and the שכינה rests there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי permits, for רבי יוסי used to say: They only prohibited it when one can see, in a place where there is no fence, and at a time when the שכינה rests there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the first opinion and permits facing any direction, except under specific conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי applies the same three limits that רבי יוחנן used for the משנה: seeing, no fence, and the שכינה being present. Outside those conditions, for example today when there is no מקדש, he permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: They only prohibited in the case of...

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei permits.
For Rabbi Yosei used to say:
They only prohibited it when one can see,
and in a place where there is no fence,
and at a time when the Divine Presence rests there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a dissenting, lenient view on the ברייתא's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The direction prohibition applies only when one can see the מקדש, without a fence, while the שכינה rests there.

steps.title: The חכמים prohibit
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי יוסי and prohibit, even without his conditions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים prohibit.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the חכמים disagreeing with רבי יוסי and keeping the prohibition in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not accept רבי יוסי's limits. They hold that the prohibition on facing ירושלים applies even when the מקדש cannot be seen and even when the שכינה is not resting there.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views. רבי יוסי, like רבי יוחנן on the משנה, limits the respect rules to when the מקדש is visible, unblocked, and the שכינה is present. The חכמים prohibit facing ירושלים even without those conditions.

phrases.english: And the Sages prohibit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יוסי, closing the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the חכמים, the prohibition stands even without seeing the מקדש or the presence of the שכינה.

steps.title: The חכמים seem identical to the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the view of the חכמים seems to be exactly the same as the view of the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The view of the חכמים is the same as the first תנא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem with the ברייתא we just learned. Both the תנא קמא and the חכמים forbid, so why list them as two separate opinions?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא does not list two opinions unless they disagree about something. Both the תנא קמא and the חכמים forbid even without רבי יוסי's conditions, so they look identical. The גמרא wants to find the practical difference between them.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages; the majority opinion quoted at the end
The first, unnamed teacher in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: The Rabbis are the same as the first Tanna!
phrases.notes: A standard challenge: two opinions that look identical.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the listing of the חכמים (Step 32) as separate from the תנא קמא (Step 30).
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's presentation of the חכמים as a separate opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both forbid, so there seems to be no difference, and the separate listing looks redundant.

steps.title: They differ about the 'sides'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא and the חכמים differ about locations off to the side, which are not directly in line with ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: the sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by naming a practical difference: places that are off to the side of ירושלים rather than directly in line with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take a place in יהודה that is not directly east or west of ירושלים, or a place in the גליל that is not directly north of it. On one explanation, the תנא קמא forbids there too, but the חכמים permit. So the two opinions really are different.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
Sides; places not directly in line with ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: 'צדדין' does not mean the side directions of the body. It means geographic locations off to the side of ירושלים.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: the sides.
phrases.notes: Places in יהודה not directly east/west of ירושלים, or in the גליל not directly north of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference (נפקא מינה) between the two opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים and the תנא קמא hold exactly the same view.
steps.terutzMaskana: They disagree about locations off to the side: the תנא קמא forbids and the חכמים permit.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: יהודה and the גליל
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא rules: in יהודה, face north-south and not east-west. In the גליל, north-south is forbidden and east-west is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: one who relieves himself in יהודה should not face east and west, only north and south. In the גליל, north and south is forbidden and east and west is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא on the same topic. This step gives its first, unnamed opinion, and the other views follow in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on where you are compared to ירושלים. In יהודה, facing east or west would line up with ירושלים, so one must face north-south instead. The גליל is north of ירושלים, so facing north-south there would line up with the מקדש, and east-west is the allowed direction.

keyTerms.meaning: Judea, the region of ירושלים, where east-west lines up with ירושלים

phrases.english: Another Baraita teaches:
One who relieves himself in Judea —
should not relieve himself facing east and west,
but rather north and south.
And in the Galilee, north and south is forbidden,
east and west is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a second ברייתא on the same topic as Steps 30-32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In יהודה face north-south only. In the גליל face east-west only.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: only where one can see
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי permits, because in his view the prohibition applies only where one can see the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי permits, for רבי יוסי used to say: they forbade it only where one can see.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יוסי's view, which disagrees with the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the direction matters only if the מקדש is actually visible from where the person is. Far away in most of יהודה or the גליל, there is no prohibition.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei permits.
For Rabbi Yosei used to say:
They forbade it only where one can see (the Temple).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting view within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prohibition applies only where the מקדש is visible.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only while the בית המקדש stands
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the prohibition applies only while the בית המקדש is standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: when the בית המקדש is standing, it is forbidden. When the בית המקדש is not standing, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a third view. רבי יהודה makes the rule depend on time, not on place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי limits the rule by distance, to where one can see. רבי יהודה limits it by time: once the בית המקדש is destroyed, there is no prohibition at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
When the Temple is standing, it is forbidden;

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: when the Temple is not standing, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another view to the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prohibition applies only while the בית המקדש stands.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: forbidden everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא forbids facing east-west in every place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא forbids it in every place.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי עקיבא, who holds the strictest view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not limit the prohibition by seeing, by time, or by region. He forbids facing east-west anywhere.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva forbids (facing east-west) in every place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final and strictest view in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Facing east-west is forbidden everywhere.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא seems identical to the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי עקיבא's view seems to be the same as the תנא קמא's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא is the same as the first תנא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same kind of question as before: the תנא קמא also forbids, so how is רבי עקיבא different?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids east-west in יהודה, and רבי עקיבא forbids east-west too. It looks as if there is no real disagreement, so the גמרא asks for the difference.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva is the same as the first Tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same challenge pattern as Step 33, now applied to the second ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Listing רבי עקיבא separately from the תנא קמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both forbid, so the separate listing seems redundant.

steps.title: They differ about חוץ לארץ
steps.stepSummary: The difference is חוץ לארץ: רבי עקיבא forbids even outside ארץ ישראל, and the תנא קמא does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by naming the practical difference: places outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא spoke only about יהודה and the גליל, places inside ארץ ישראל. רבי עקיבא's words 'in every place' include even חוץ לארץ, so there too one may not face east-west.
steps.whatToRemember: In the second ברייתא, the views run from most lenient to most strict: רבי יוסי (only where one can see), רבי יהודה (only while the מקדש stands), the תנא קמא (inside ארץ ישראל), and רבי עקיבא (everywhere, even חוץ לארץ).

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: outside the Land (of Israel).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 39.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא and the תנא קמא hold the same view.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא forbids even outside ארץ ישראל. The תנא קמא's rule is limited to ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: אביי moves רבה's bricks
steps.stepSummary: In רבה's bathroom the bricks were set east-west. אביי turned them north-south, and רבה came in and put them back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה's bathroom bricks were placed east and west. אביי went and turned them north and south. רבה came in and fixed them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבה's practice. It is setting up רבה's statement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bricks were arranged so that רבה would sit facing north-south. אביי moved them to test whether this was on purpose or just by chance. רבה fixing them shows it was deliberate.

keyTerms.meaning: He fixed them, set them right

phrases.english: For Rabba, they would place for him
the bricks east and west.
phrases.notes: So that he would sit facing north-south.

phrases.english: Abaye went and placed them north and south,
phrases.notes: To test whether רבה was particular.

phrases.english: Rabba entered and fixed them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה הֲווֹ שַׁדְיָין לֵיהּ לִבְנֵי מִזְרָח וּמַעֲרָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing how the view of רבי עקיבא was practiced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה was careful about the direction of his bathroom even in בבל.

steps.title: רבה: I hold like רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבה says: who is bothering me? I hold like רבי עקיבא, who forbids in every place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Who is this who is bothering me? I hold like רבי עקיבא, who said it is forbidden in every place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains why he fixed the bricks: he follows רבי עקיבא's strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה lived in בבל, outside ארץ ישראל. That is exactly the case where רבי עקיבא differs from the תנא קמא (Step 40). By being strict there, רבה shows he truly follows רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: I hold, I am of the opinion

steps.whatToRemember: רבה, living in בבל, followed רבי עקיבא and avoided facing east-west even outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: The story turns רבי עקיבא's view from theory into actual practice by a major אמורא, in exactly the case (חוץ לארץ) where his view makes a difference.

phrases.english: He said: Who is this who is upsetting me?
I hold in accordance with Rabbi Akiva,
who said: It is forbidden in every place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story of Step 41 with רבה's explanation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבה rules like רבי עקיבא: facing east-west while relieving oneself is forbidden everywhere, even in בבל.
